messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT realtime p95/p99 regression detected in us-west-1 for /v1/realtime-stream. p95 150ms -> 520ms, p99 600ms -> 3.8s. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/11023 paging @taylor
Taylor Ng: I'm on it. Pulling dashboards and recent deploys. Ravi, any customer complaints?
Ravi Desai: support shows a small spike in streaming trouble tickets: two customers reporting frame skips and elevated client-side timeouts. Estimates ~2.4% of sessions affected. Sending initial message to affected customers.
Sasha Green: infra shows a burst of pending pods in the streaming pool and a pattern of OOMKill + rapid recycle on a subset of runners. Also seeing increased docker image pulls failing intermittently.
Maya Patel: runtime metrics: big KV cache miss wave starting ~3m ago; model-serving worker processes show repeated GC pauses and high RSS. Also a recent control-plane rollout changed default_batch_timeout for streaming (slightly higher) — curious.
Taylor Ng: check recent deploys in the region.
Sasha Green: ```
# curl -s https://ci.redwood/api/recent-deploys?env=us-west-1 | jq '.[0:6]'
[
  {"id": 4121, "service": "control-plane", "time": "2027-03-04T19:18:02Z", "user": "deploy-bot", "desc": "feat: streaming routing flags"},
  {"id": 4119, "service": "streaming-runtime", "time": "2027-03-04T18:54:10Z", "user": "maya", "desc": "tune: default_batch_timeout -> 120ms"}
]
```
Ravi Desai: support note: customers 'pixelflux' and 'datawave' reported stalls with reconnects. They're monitoring and want ETA.
Taylor Ng: immediate mitigations candidate list: 1) scale up streaming pool, 2) force-route a small canary to quantized model pool, 3) revert the batch timeout tweak, 4) cordon noisy nodes. Execute in parallel: Ravi handle comms, Sasha take nodes, Maya handle runtime flags, I'll coordinate routing/scale.
Sasha Green: cordoning worker-104 and worker-107 now, draining non-critical pods. `kubectl cordon worker-104 && kubectl drain worker-104 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Maya Patel: applying runtime safeguard: lower max_batch_size from 96 -> 48 for streaming pool via feature flag: `redwoodctl set runtime.streaming.max_batch_size=48 --region us-west-1`
Taylor Ng: initiating routing fallback to quantized model (model-v2-q) as 12% canary: `curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood/api/routes/override -d '{"route":"/v1/realtime-stream","target_pool":"model-v2-q","canary_pct":12,"reason":"p99 spike us-west"}'`
ops-bot: Action logged: route-override-20270304 by taylor  https://ci.redwood/builds/4124
Sasha Green: kube events show imagepull issues around the time of spike: `ImagePullBackOff` on several pods. Also seeing `Evicted` due to MemoryPressure.
Sasha Green: ```
# kubectl get events -n streaming | tail -n 30
2027-03-04T19:20:11Z Warning ImagePullBackOff pod/runner-abcde registry-401
2027-03-04T19:21:05Z Warning Evicted pod/streamer-xyz MemoryPressure
2027-03-04T19:21:15Z Normal Scheduled pod/streamer-new Node/worker-110
```
Maya Patel: after batch_size cap and canary, canary p99 dropped to ~880ms. Global p99 trending down but still noisy. The KV cache miss rate has started to recover on nodes we restarted.
Ravi Desai: sent customer update: "We've applied a temporary routing fallback and increased capacity. Expect improvement in 10 minutes; monitoring closely. We'll follow up with a postmortem."
Taylor Ng: Sasha, status on cordoned nodes? Any hardware NIC errors or disk pressure?
Sasha Green: worker-104 had high RSS and OOMKill cycles; worker-107 had disk pressure from a failed shard download. Infra team investigating registry auth flaps. I've left both cordoned until infra confirms.
infra-bot: Registry team notified: investigating intermittent 401s during shard pulls in us-west-1 around 19:20Z.
Taylor Ng: scaling action: bumping min replicas for streaming pool by +25% for 30m: `redwoodctl scale pool streaming-usw1 --min-replicas 16` -> success.
ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20270304-58. Postmortem draft created at https://docs.redwood/incident/INC-20270304-58/postmortem
Maya Patel: runtime logs show fewer KV eviction cycles after restarts. Suggest we also reduce prefetch to avoid large working set: `redwoodctl set runtime.streaming.prefetch=false --region us-west-1`
Taylor Ng: done. Also enabling an emergency auto-fallback in control-plane for p99 > 2s: temporary threshold change. `curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood/api/flags -d '{"fallback_on_p99":2000}'`
Taylor Ng: note: the fallback policy didn't auto-trigger initially because control-plane was configured to trigger only on error_rate, not tail latency. We'll note that for postmortem.
Ravi Desai: customers ack'd improvements; pixelflux says frames improved, datawave confirms lower timeouts.
Sasha Green: infra reports registry token rotation completed; ImagePullBackOffs clearing and new pods coming up. Uncordoning worker-107 once pod churn subsides.
Maya Patel: warning: once traffic ramps we might see re-eviction. I'll add a temporary soft memory limit to the runtime process to avoid full cache wipe: `kubectl set env deployment/streaming-runtime RUNTIME_MEM_SOFT_LIMIT=0.75`
Taylor Ng: good. Any remaining hotspots?
Sasha Green: worker-110 still reports elevated RSS but stable. No new OOMs in the last 5m.
ops-bot: MONITOR: p99 <= 1.2s sustained for 15m window. Current p99 1.05s.
Taylor Ng: containment summary for ticket: scale + route canary + cap batch_size + cordon noisy nodes + runtime prefetch off + registry token rotate. Outcome: p99 reduced from 3.8s -> 1.05s within ~10 minutes.
Ravi Desai: I'm taking 30m watch and will coordinate customer follow-ups and the postmortem communications. Taylor, please add technical action owners to the ticket.
Maya Patel: post-incident action items: - change control-plane fallback trigger to include tail latency thresholds - add deploy guard to prevent batch_size increases > X without region approval - implement RUNTIME_MEM_SOFT_LIMIT behavior to avoid full KV eviction - improve registry pull token renewal alerts
Taylor Ng: assigning Sasha for infra follow-up (registry), Maya for runtime guard changes, and Ravi for customer comms. I'll own control-plane fallback change.
ops-bot: Postmortem draft updated with action items: https://docs.redwood/incident/INC-20270304-58/postmortem
Taylor Ng: handing off watch to Ravi for customer comms and monitoring. If p99 climbs above 2s or any more OOMs occur, ping with @oncall and escalate to SRE lead.
Ravi Desai: acknowledged, taking handoff.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT MONITORING: p99 < 1.2s for 15m. Current p99 1.03s.
Ravi Desai: closing slack thread; continuing investigation and postmortem in INC-20270304-58. Thanks all for fast coordination. :thumbsup:
